note: PLAT-001 run Windows x86_64: the smoke runs on the actual host and asserts what the native platform did rather than what a fixture expects. A program is published into a store as an artifact, installed as a profile generation, and run through the profile runner; the program is the built client itself, so the product starts itself natively and answers a subcommand. A second generation is installed and the profile is rolled back to the first, with the active generation read back and compared both ways, so a rollback that silently stayed put would be caught. Platform details come from the product's own host detection (windows/x86_64) rather than from a constant in the test. The build half of the case is covered by the packaging backends' native cases. Fault proof: making rollback report success without moving the active pointer fails the rollback assertion (exit 1); revert byte-identical against a backup, no FAULT markers remain. Recorded on the host platform.
authority: self-reported local review, not independent attestation
